beats.text: Your coding agent asks before it touches anything. Starting Friday, Anthropic is turning that prompt off by default, and its argument is that the prompt was the risky part.
beats.show_cue: Operator's own screen showing a real Claude Code permission prompt, the thing that is about to disappear.
curiosity_queries: TechCrunch Anthropic Claude Code auto mode article
Claude Code terminal approval prompt demo

beats.text: From now, the agent edits files and runs commands while a built in checker screens every move. Anthropic's own test watched 1,053 people use it. The checker caught 89 percent of risky commands. The humans clicked allow on almost everything, catching 13.6.
beats.show_cue: The vendor's own post held on the plan names, then the results chart, 13.6 versus 89, with the 1,053 testers footnote visible.

beats.text: The team's own lead posted the change himself, no hedge needed there. Click yes two hundred times and the two hundred and first isn't a decision anymore. It's a reflex.
beats.show_cue: The first party post held full frame, then a fast cut of a hand clicking allow, allow, allow.

beats.text: But that's the company's own study, on the company's own product, with no outside audit anyone can check. And a default that removes a prompt also removes the moment you'd have noticed something wrong.
